title: CDP redirect interceptor (registration_cdp.py) is proven only against a fake CDP client, never real Chrome
evidence: Unit tests drive RedirectInterceptor and PageCdp with fakes. Unverified in Chrome: second CDP websocket on the page target alongside chromedriver; Fetch.continueResponse following a 3xx at response stage; networkId continuity across hops; Fetch events for fetch(no-cors) under the DNR policy and script-execution-disabled; 5 s command timeout. Failure mode is uncertain (fail closed), not a leak.
fix_direction: When no other agent is driving Chrome, run a real-Chrome case against a local fixture: 302 to same host (expect submitted), 302 to second approved loopback host (submitted), 307/308 to localhost not in allowedHosts and 307 to a second approved host (expect zero POSTs at the target, uncertain), CDP connect refused (expect redirect:'error' behaviour).
verification: Interceptor works in real Chrome: cases a-c pass without shim on localhost:<port>, d0 loud fallback; ownership+iframe 66/66; 10/10 maker mutants and 3 checker mutants red. Residual (socket death while a 307/308 is paused) tracked in ISS-REGCDP-002/-003.

title: If the interceptor connection dies mid-submit, Chrome resumes paused requests and a 307/308 to a different approved host could be followed
evidence: On CDP client disconnect Chrome releases paused Fetch requests. The DNR allow-list still blocks unapproved hosts; only the same-host rule for body-resending redirects is lost. verdict() downgrades to uncertain but cannot unsend.
fix_direction: Consider keeping redirect:'error' unless the approved-host list has a single host, or add a second DNR rule set scoped to the submit window; decide with the owner.

title: Enabling the interceptor switches the page fetch to redirect:'follow': interceptor death, hang or Fetch.disable/close hands redirect decisions back to Chrome with DNR as the only remaining guard
evidence: submit_with_redirects passes redirectMode='follow' whenever Fetch.enable was acked. Paused requests are released by Chrome when the CDP client disconnects or Fetch.disable runs. Reachable: a response-stage pause left unanswered (5 s send timeout, then failRequest also times out) outlives the 10 s script timeout, then stop() closes and Chrome follows the 3xx. Unapproved hosts are still stopped by the persistent DNR block-all/allow-approved rules (re-verified by policy_check just before submit); an approved second host via 307/308 is not (ISS-REGCDP-002). Handler EXCEPTIONS fail closed (tested, mutation-killed); transport loss does not.
fix_direction: Owner decision: accept DNR as the backstop (documented), or restrict follow mode to origins with one approved host, or use a cancel-on-timeout wrapper that calls Fetch.failRequest for every still-paused id before close. Cover with the real-Chrome run in ISS-REGCDP-001.

title: Protected positive-alias fixture (D-110/D-111: approved alias 307 re-sends body, expects 2 POSTs) now asserts ONE POST and uncertain; owner-approved positive behaviour no longer reachable
evidence: Base test expected POST /submit then POST /redirected on the approved alias (cookies [auth, None]). Since regsafe 87df0d1f (redirect:'error') that was already unreachable; T-052 deliberately refuses 307/308 to another approved host (body_resend_other_host). Cycle 1 rewrote the expectation to match. Stricter, not a leak, but a D-111 positive control was changed without an owner decision.
fix_direction: Owner decides: ratify the same-host-only 307/308 rule (then record an amendment so D-110/D-111 no longer promise the alias positive) or permit 307/308 to another APPROVED host under the interceptor (same trade-off as ISS-REGCDP-002).
